slides.title: Preparing the sediment slide
bullets: 1. Mix the urine and pour 10–15 mL into a centrifuge tube; balance the tubes in the centrifuge.
2. Centrifuge for 5 minutes at medium speed (Kurbonova: 3000 rpm).
3. Pour off the supernatant carefully (Kurbonova: leave 1 mL of sediment); shake the tube so that the sediment mixes evenly with the remaining liquid.
4. Put a drop of sediment on a slide with a pipette; holding the cover glass by a corner, lower it gently so that no bubbles form.
5. Do not let the preparation dry out — examine it at once.
6. If there is no centrifuge, let the urine stand for a while to obtain a sediment.

slides.title: Microscopy
bullets: 1. Partly close the condenser to limit the light; with the 10× objective look for red cells, white cells, epithelial cells, casts and other elements. A coloured filter may be used.
2. To identify casts and salt crystals use the 40× objective (400× magnification).
3. Identify all cellular elements, yeasts, the type of casts, bacteria and crystals, and record everything found.
4. Even if 1–2 casts or crystals per field at low power have no diagnostic value, record them, especially when kidney stones are suspected.
5. Do not mistake foreign objects (wool, plant pollen, cotton fibres, air bubbles, starch grains) for elements.

slides.title: Sediment elements: cells and micro-organisms
rows: Small yellowish pale-green discs; darker edges, sometimes spiky
If many — bacterial infection, kidney tumour or stones, endocarditis, prostate or clotting-system disease
Granular discs, nucleus sometimes visible; broken-down forms, pus
If many — urinary-tract infection, pyelonephritis, kidney tuberculosis
Large irregular cells, clear granules, nucleus usually visible
Many cells indicate that collection rules were not followed, or urinary-tract infection
The smallest epithelial cells, about twice the size of a white cell, granular nucleus
Nephritis, necrotic syndrome, acute renal failure
Usually rods, sometimes cocci or streptococci
In fresh urine they indicate urinary-tract infection
Colourless small round or oval cells; may be budding; do not mistake for red cells
The size of a white cell, four flagella, move fast in fresh urine

slides.title: Casts
rows: No diagnostic value in the normal range; may occur in healthy people after exertion
Short, wide, smooth, crumble easily, dull or yellowish
Severe kidney disease, progressive renal failure
Made of broken-down red cells; orange-red or whitish
Parallel edges, blunt ends; made of broken-down white cells
Short, granules from broken-down cells, yellowish
Degenerative processes in the kidney, severe kidney pathology
Larger than white-cell casts; cells usually in two rows
Acute tubular failure, pyelonephritis, interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis

slides.title: Crystals
rows: In alkaline medium the surface is feathery
Urates — yellow, phosphates — white small spheres

slides.title: Sources of error and interpretation
bullets: If urine stands for more than an hour after collection, red cells lyse and casts break down.
Kurbonova: normally up to 5–6 white cells and 0–2 red cells per field, no casts; Aripova writes that red cells are not normally present (except in samples taken during menstruation).
Dirt on cover glasses and slides and foreign objects from the air (wool, pollen, cotton fibres) may be mistaken for sediment elements.

In the Nechiporenko method the formed elements in 1 mL of urine are counted in a Goryaev chamber; calculation formulas and reference values differ between the sources, so follow the laboratory’s instructions.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Wear single-use gloves when handling specimens; after work wash the hands with soap or wipe them with an alcohol solution.
Balance the tubes in the centrifuge; close the lid and do not open it until the machine has stopped completely.
Put used containers, tubes and slides into a disinfectant solution (concentration and time according to the regulation in force).
